title: Change guardrails: release endorsement lifecycle for shadow canaries and automated rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement an end-to-end endorsement and change-management lifecycle for model rollouts that covers shadow traffic, canary/A-B experiments, and automated rollback triggers. The goal is to provide clear RBAC mappings, required approvers by risk tier, evidence bundling for audits, and Console integrations so product teams can run progressive rollouts with predictable governance and minimal manual overhead. This initiative should work across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments and tie into existing observability and incident workflows.
tasks: Draft risk taxonomy for rollout changes (feature, model variant, hyperparam/quantization, runtime config)
Specify approval matrix: roles required for low/medium/high risk changes and delegation expiry rules
Design audit artifact format: evidence bundle linking prompt evals, PRs, dashboards, and trace ids
Define automated rollback policy DSL and threshold primitives (latency p95, error rate increase, regression on evaluation prompts)
Implement Console UI hooks: endorse/deny buttons, evidence viewer, and delegation config
Backend: RBAC enforcement endpoints and immutable audit log entries for each step
Integrate with existing Canary engine to allow shadowing rules and split traffic configuration
End-to-end runbook and emergency bypass procedure for on-call during partial outages
Create QA and integration tests that simulate metric drift and verify rollback and audit creation
acceptance_criteria: Approval matrix defined and published in Confluence with examples for each risk tier
RBAC rules enforce required approvers for a rollout change in both Console and API
Automated rollback can be configured per rollout and triggers within specified thresholds in a canary run using synthetic and production signals
Audit artifacts are emitted as an immutable bundle (links + metadata) stored in the audit index and viewable in Console
Shadow traffic experiments can be declared as part of the rollout with separate reviewer requirements and do not count toward production quotas until endorsed
Delegated approvals expire after configurable TTL and are visible in the audit trail
Playbook validated by on-call by running a simulated canary regression and confirming rollback, escalation, and incident ticket creation
